summary.oneLiner: V-Mart Retail is an organised value-fashion retailer offering apparel, footwear, home furnishings and general merchandise at compelling prices, focused on Tier-II/III/IV cities and India's aspiring middle class.
summary.business: V-Mart Retail operates an omnichannel value-retailing business selling apparel (ethnic, fusion and western wear for women; formal, casual and sportswear for men; children's apparel across age groups), footwear, home furnishings and general merchandise, plus retail trading of FMCG, through 577 physical stores and digital/marketplace channels. It targets budget-conscious, fashion-seeking young middle-class families and young adults in Tier-II, III and IV Indian cities, complementing its store network (LimeRoad) with an omnichannel ecosystem for discovery, transaction and fulfilment.

risks.note: The Indian retail ecosystem is evolving rapidly with rising competition from organised players, regional retailers and digital-first brands, which may impact V-Mart's market share and pricing dynamics; mitigated by enhancing in-store experience, sharpening the price-value proposition and merchandise quality/relevance.

Geopolitical developments, logistics challenges, raw material constraints and input-cost fluctuations may disrupt sourcing, impact product availability and pressure cost structures; mitigated via a diversified supply network, strategic vendor partnerships and data-driven inventory/warehousing improvements.

Increasing climate-related events, including extreme weather, pose risks to infrastructure, supply chain continuity and store operations, potentially impacting business resilience; mitigated by integrating climate considerations into supply chain/merchandising and strengthening Business Continuity Management.

Seasonal demand cycles and working capital requirements may influence the Company's liquidity and cash conversion efficiency; mitigated through disciplined working capital management, optimised cash flows and improved inventory efficiency via data-driven systems.

Rapid changes in consumer behaviour, driven by evolving fashion trends, cultural shifts, digital exposure and inflationary pressure, require continuous adaptation to remain relevant; mitigated by accelerating the design-to-market cycle and strengthening entry-price offerings and digital/data-led merchandising.

The evolving, competitive talent landscape and the rise of AI require reimagining workforce capabilities; the Company is building a future-ready, AI-enabled workforce through learning, inclusion, career development, competitive rewards and performance-linked systems.

Increasing digitalisation exposes the Company to cybersecurity risks that may affect data integrity, operational continuity and stakeholder confidence; mitigated through advanced security systems, real-time threat monitoring, and regular vulnerability/penetration testing.

one-line thesis: V-Mart delivered record Q4 FY26 sales growth (24%) and EBITDA growth (56%) driven by disciplined store expansion, AI-powered loss reduction in LimeRoad, and improved inventory health, with PAT rising 6x to INR124cr; the key change is sustainable margin recovery toward pre-COVID levels despite raw material inflation, and what matters is the company’s ability to pass on only 1-2% price increases while maintaining footfall and repeat customer loyalty (72% of sales).
financial scorecard: revenue: +24% YoY; EBITDA/margin: +56% YoY to INR106cr, margin +220bps to 10.9% (one-off: LimeRoad commission income down 12% impacted gross margin); PAT (rptd): INR10cr (Q4); PAT (normalized): INR124cr (FY26, 6x YoY, after reversing INR1cr exceptional charge from prior quarter); order book: Not disclosed; net debt: Zero long-term debt, positive FCF of INR33cr YTD vs negative INR33cr last year
guidance: revenue growth: 13-15% area expansion annually; margin: Targeting pre-COVID PAT margin levels (4-4.5%) in medium term; order inflow: 50-60% of FY27 fabric needs pre-booked; capex/commissioning: FY27 capex estimated at INR170-180cr (vs INR159cr FY26), primarily for tech/AI investments and store refurbishments
order book & pipeline: 50-60% of FY27 fabric requirements pre-booked through vendor partnerships; no formal order book disclosed
segment / subsidiary detail: V-Mart: 12% LTL; Unlimited: 9% LTL, 28% revenue growth, 63% EBITDA growth; LimeRoad: Marketplace loss reduced significantly, now CM3 profitable in high single digits, driving omni-channel loyalty and higher repeat rates
growth verticals / optionality: South India (Tamil Nadu, Karnataka) expansion under Unlimited format; omni-channel integration via LimeRoad; international fabric sourcing to mitigate supply chain risks; AI-driven design and inventory optimization
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin down 100bps YoY due to LimeRoad commission decline (12%) and inventory provision; underlying gross margin improving due to fresher inventory, lower discounting, and higher full-price sell-through; apparel ASP up 5% due to festive mix and kurta sets; raw material inflation (yarn +10-15%) translates to 3-4% garment cost increase, partially absorbed (1-2%) and partially passed on
capex / expansion: FY26: INR159cr (new stores, refurbishments, tech); FY27 guidance: INR170-180cr; incremental spend driven by AI/tech investments (not store count)
capital allocation: Zero debt; all growth funded internally via FCF; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; focus on reinvestment in tech, inventory, and store expansion
risks & watch-items: Raw material inflation (polyester/crude-linked); labor cost increases post-Haryana/Noida wage hikes; supply chain disruptions from geopolitical events and labor shortages in Tamil Nadu/Bengal; consumer sentiment erosion if inflation persists; competitive store openings in saturated markets
management quality / tone: Confident, optimistic, and operationally disciplined; management emphasizes sustainability over short-term gains, highlights AI and efficiency, acknowledges inflation risks but downplays demand erosion due to loyal customer base (72% repeat); tone is calm, data-driven, and focused on long-term ROC targets (15-18% → 20%+)
non-obvious takeaways: LimeRoad’s profitability at CM3 level validates its role as a loyalty engine, not just a marketplace; 72% sales from repeat customers is unusually high for value retail and underpins pricing power; AI is being used for loss prevention (70% reduction) and inventory optimization, not just chatbots

themes.title: Quick-commerce, omnichannel & retail expansion
themes.need: Quick-commerce and value retail are the structural growth engine, and Q1FY27 rewrote the unit-economics model. ETERNAL raised Blinkit's steady-state margin from a 5-6% range to ~6% and set a first-ever 4% GAAP EBIT margin target (after ESOP and depreciation) while capex per store went from INR 1cr to INR 2.5cr (+150%) with NOV/store/day up only 60% and net working capital improving 18 to 14 days - so margin can now drift DOWN while ROCE improves. Growth also decoupled from spend: Blinkit orders +21% QoQ with MTUs above 30mn achieved on LOWER marketing spend and fewer store adds, and management called Q1 the peak of competitive intensity to date. VMM did INR 3,727cr (+18.7%) on 10% SSSG with gross margin up to 28.7% driven by lower promotional spend rather than price hikes, validated a small-format store at the same revenue/sq ft and 'pretty much the same' ROCE as large format (a ~3,000-store national opportunity), and found 20% of its quick-commerce customers had never shopped a Vishal store. SHOPERSTOP swung PAT positive (+INR 5cr vs -INR 4cr) and raised FY27 LFL guidance from 5% to ~6%; ARVINDFASN lifted gross margin 90bps to 56.7% on full-price sell-through with direct channels now 62% of sales; MEESHO cut cost per delivered order ~INR 1 QoQ despite the May fuel hike. DMART/V2RETAIL/PATELRMART on value retail; TRENT-tier branded retail via ABFRL/METROBRAND/BATAINDIA/REDTAPE.
themes.driver: Blinkit dark-store rollout at the new INR 2.5cr/store capex against the 4% GAAP EBIT target; VMM small-format expansion; festive/quick-commerce GMV. Watch ARVINDFASN's SS27 sourcing lock (next 45-60 days) - if war-inflated input costs hold, apparel pricing corrects.

hero.oneLiner: V-Mart Retail is an organised value-fashion retailer offering apparel, footwear, home furnishings and general merchandise at compelling prices, focused on Tier-II/III/IV cities and India's aspiring middle class.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: V-Mart Retail is an organised value-fashion retailer offering apparel, footwear, home furnishings and general merchandise at compelling prices, focused on Tier-II/III/IV cities and India's aspiring middle class.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: V-Mart Retail operates an omnichannel value-retailing business selling apparel (ethnic, fusion and western wear for women; formal, casual and sportswear for men; children's apparel across age groups), footwear, home furnishings and general merchandise, plus retail trading of FMCG, through 577 physical stores and digital/marketplace channels. It targets budget-conscious, fashion-seeking young middle-class families and young adults in Tier-II, III and IV Indian cities, complementing its store network (LimeRoad) with an omnichannel ecosystem for discovery, transaction and fulfilment.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: V-Mart: 12% LTL; Unlimited: 9% LTL, 28% revenue growth, 63% EBITDA growth; LimeRoad: Marketplace loss reduced significantly, now CM3 profitable in high single digits, driving omni-channel loyalty and higher repeat rates

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Apparel (79% of turnover):** Women's ethnic, fusion and western wear, Men's formal, casual and sportswear, Children's apparel across age groups
- **Non-Apparel (10% of turnover):** Footwear, Home furnishings, General merchandise
- **FMCG (11% of turnover):** Retail trading of FMCG
- **Private labels:** 9 private-label brands, contributing ~66-70% of revenue

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Tier-II, Tier-III and Tier-IV cities across India
- 577 stores across 28 states/UTs and 328 cities
- Digital/omnichannel presence across ~22,000 pin codes (via LimeRoad and marketplaces)
- Domestic only — company does not export any goods or services

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: 50-60% of FY27 fabric requirements pre-booked through vendor partnerships; no formal order book disclosed

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: revenue growth: 13-15% area expansion annually; margin: Targeting pre-COVID PAT margin levels (4-4.5%) in medium term; order inflow: 50-60% of FY27 fabric needs pre-booked; capex/commissioning: FY27 capex estimated at INR170-180cr (vs INR159cr FY26), primarily for tech/AI investments and store refurbishments

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: South India (Tamil Nadu, Karnataka) expansion under Unlimited format; omni-channel integration via LimeRoad; international fabric sourcing to mitigate supply chain risks; AI-driven design and inventory optimization

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's rapidly expanding middle-income population (expected to reach ~715 million by 2030) is increasing discretionary spending on apparel, lifestyle and consumer goods, seeking quality at accessible prices.
- Technology and phygital retail models are connecting digital discovery with in-store engagement; India's e-commerce market is projected to grow at an 11.5% CAGR (2025-2029) to USD 326.7 billion by 2029.
- Non-metro (Tier-II/III) markets are powering demand, with over 60% of e-commerce demand originating from non-metros, becoming critical drivers of organised retail expansion.
- Value fashion segment is driving market expansion; the Indian apparel retail market is expected to reach ~Rs. 16 lakh crore by FY 2029-30 (per CARE Ratings), with value/affordable formats driving store expansion.
- Organised retail penetration is rising structurally (15% in 2018 to 21% in 2024, projected 35% by 2030), implying a USD 600 billion+ opportunity by 2030.
- Private consumption accounts for 61.5% of India's GDP (First Advance Estimates), underpinning domestic demand-led growth; real GDP growth for FY 2026-27 projected at 6.6%, broadly in line with India's ~7% potential growth rate.
- A late-FY26 oil price shock (Iran-US conflict, Strait of Hormuz disruption) poses upside risk to inflation, input costs and external balances, with its full macroeconomic impact expected in the subsequent period.
- Management's response to these demand trends: strengthening digital capabilities, deepening presence in non-metros via cluster-led store expansion, disciplined sourcing, tighter quality control, private-label expansion and continuous merchandise innovation.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross margin down 100bps YoY due to LimeRoad commission decline (12%) and inventory provision; underlying gross margin improving due to fresher inventory, lower discounting, and higher full-price sell-through; apparel ASP up 5% due to festive mix and kurta sets; raw material inflation (yarn +10-15%) translates to 3-4% garment cost increase, partially absorbed (1-2%) and partially passed on

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Zero debt; all growth funded internally via FCF; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; focus on reinvestment in tech, inventory, and store expansion

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: V-Mart pursued a cluster-led store expansion strategy, adding 92 new stores in FY 2025-26 (highest-ever new store additions) to reach a network of 577 stores across 328 cities in 28 states/UTs, increasing retail area by ~16% and deepening presence in Tier-II, III and IV markets. The store network spans ~50 lakh sq. ft. of retail space, supported by 2 warehouses. Per the Value Creation Model 'Inputs' disclosure, capital expenditure for the year was Rs. 15,918 Lakhs, directed largely toward this store network expansion together with digital/technology infrastructure (Digital Spine, PLM, warehouse automation and PTL infrastructure).

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, optimistic, and operationally disciplined; management emphasizes sustainability over short-term gains, highlights AI and efficiency, acknowledges inflation risks but downplays demand erosion due to loyal customer base (72% repeat); tone is calm, data-driven, and focused on long-term ROC targets (15-18% → 20%+)

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Extensive pan-India presence catering to diverse and evolving consumer segments across Tier-II/III/IV cities
- Strong value-for-money proposition with average selling price of ~₹350, targeted at families with monthly incomes of ₹20,000–₹50,000
- Diverse product portfolio spanning apparel, footwear, accessories, home offerings and aspirational FMCG
- Private labels contribute ~66-70% of revenue, enabling sharper design control, margin capture and regional relevance
- Large-scale sourcing capabilities supported by dedicated design labs for trend-led collections; relationship ecosystem of 400+ vendors
- Cluster-led store expansion strategy enabling localised market responsiveness in underserved high-growth urban and semi-urban markets
- Technology backbone — a unified 'Digital Spine' integrating product, inventory, store and customer data — enabling near real-time visibility, predictive planning and 84% season sell-through with 66-67% forecast accuracy
- Scalable and resilient supply chain; compressed order-to-shelf cycle from ~80 days to 70-75 days via PLM and Design-to-Display digitisation
- High customer loyalty (72% repeat purchases) and satisfaction (Google rating 4.9; NPS 85%)
- Debt-free at the standalone operating level per management commentary, cash-generative growth

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Raw material inflation (polyester/crude-linked); labor cost increases post-Haryana/Noida wage hikes; supply chain disruptions from geopolitical events and labor shortages in Tamil Nadu/Bengal; consumer sentiment erosion if inflation persists; competitive store openings in saturated markets

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: LimeRoad’s profitability at CM3 level validates its role as a loyalty engine, not just a marketplace; 72% sales from repeat customers is unusually high for value retail and underpins pricing power; AI is being used for loss prevention (70% reduction) and inventory optimization, not just chatbots

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Five strategic pillars: Profitable & Capital-Disciplined Growth, Stable & Scalable Operating Model, AI-Augmented System-Driven Enterprise, Customer-Centric Competitive Advantage, and Future-Ready, Productive & Well-Governed Enterprise.
- Cluster-led store expansion strategy focused on Tier-II, III and IV cities and underserved, high-growth urban/semi-urban markets.
- Volume-led growth while maintaining pricing discipline and consumer value.
- Strengthening hyper-local merchandise planning through a mix of in-house and curated regional brands, growing private-label/in-house brand …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [M&A history] Growth includes two acquisitions the deck footnotes repeatedly: "acquisition of 74 store of Unlimited in FY22 and acquisition of LimeRoad.com in FY23" — FY21 and FY22 numbers are flagged as not comparable due to COVID.
- [Marketplace] LimeRoad is reported on NMV (Net Merchandise Value), not revenue: "NMV Growth: 18% YoY & Losses down: 39% YoY To ₹28 Mn", with LimeRoad Commission Income separately footnoted at ₹104 Mn (Q1 FY'26 ₹81 Mn).
- [Awards] Cited recognitions include the 24th ICSI National Awards for Excellence in Corporate Governance 2025, ICAI Silver Shield for Excellence in Financial Reporting 2026, "Globally ranked 19th best Integrated Annual Report in 2026", Golden Peacock Award 2022, Retail Brand of the Year 2024 and "India's Best Workplaces in Retail 2022, 2021 & 2020".
- [Governance] Board is chaired by a non-executive chairperson (Aakash Moondhra, former Global CFO of Naspers Fintech and PayU) with independent directors including Govind S. Shrikhande, ex-MD of Shoppers' Stop; promoters Lalit Agarwal (MD) and Madan Gopal Agarwal (Whole Time Director) hold executive roles.
- [Accounting] The deck presents a full Ind AS 116 bridge, reporting both Pre-Ind AS 116 and Post-Ind AS 116 P&L columns; right-of-use assets of ₹7,612 Mn sit against lease liabilities of ₹6,048 Mn (non-current) and ₹2,539 Mn (current) as at June 30, 2026.
